evals.name: sidebar-workspace
evals.prompt: we need our own place inside docspace for the ops team. a screen you get to from the left menu listing every room with how many people are in it - search at the top, a switch to include archived ones, and a way to order them by name or by when they were last touched. there are a few hundred rooms so don't drag all of them in at once, pull more as you go. we tick several rooms and archive them in one go, and since that takes a minute we want to watch it run somewhere that isn't a frozen dialog. clicking a room takes you into it. the same screen needs a second view with the people across those rooms and their role, so nobody has to click into every room to find out who is where. when a search finds nothing, say so properly instead of leaving a blank page. only admins get a screen under portal settings with our webhook url, an environment (production / staging / local), how often to poll in minutes and a switch for notifying on changes - saving must stay impossible while the url isn't https or the minutes aren't between 1 and 60. when someone creates or renames a room the list should notice. a small icon in the sidebar that jumps straight to the list would be nice too. half the team is on dark theme so it has to look right there.
evals.expected_output: A built module plugin with ArticleNavigation + Settings + EventListener + ArticleButton scopes. The workspace is one ArticleNavigation page pinned to Section.Files whose body is a Tabs pair: a room list and a people view. The list is a SearchInput, a sort ComboBox, an archived ToggleButton in a sized row, per-row Checkbox selection with an indeterminate select-all, RectangleSkeletons while it loads, an EmptyScreenContainer when a search matches nothing, and paged loading through usePluginAPI with count/startIndex and an AbortController. Ticked rooms are archived one by one with the floating operations button reporting progress - added once, then updated on the same id, completed at the end. The people view resolves members per room and shows the role. The settings page loads with usePluginSettings().load(), handles the never-saved null, and hands the portal its Save button through setSaveButton with isDisabled tied to both the https check and a 1-60 minutes check. The event handler takes no arguments and returns a toast plus an item update. The sidebar button is a 32x32 IconButton that navigates to the page. No hardcoded colors; react, react-dom, react/jsx-runtime, the SDK's React entry and the kit stay external.
assertions: dist/plugin.zip exists
validate-plugin.mjs --invoke reports zero errors

package.json depends on @onlyoffice/docspace-plugin-sdk 3.x - the npm range ^3.0.0 or the vendored onlyoffice-docspace-plugin-sdk-3.0.0.tgz, which is what the generator writes while the release is unpublished - and declares runtime: module
the plugin is its default export - no window.Plugins assignment
vite.config keeps react, react-dom, react/jsx-runtime, @onlyoffice/docspace-plugin-sdk/react and @docspace/ui-kit external and bundles the SDK root
ArticleNavigation, Settings, EventListener and ArticleButton scopes are declared, implemented, and each item scope registers at least one item
the workspace is a single ArticleNavigation page whose component is passed as a component, not a JSX element, with appears pinning it to Section.Files
the two views are the kit's Tabs with selectedItemId held in state and onSelect updating it - not two sidebar entries and not hand-rolled tab buttons
rooms are loaded with usePluginAPI() in a useEffect with an AbortController signal and a catch that ignores code ABORTED, not with fetch and .response

the portal calls live in per-domain modules that take the PluginAPIClient as an argument and import nothing from react, with usePluginAPI() used only in a thin per-domain hook at the boundary - not api.get() calls spread through the components

more rooms are pulled in pages - count and startIndex (or the portal's filter params) are passed to /files/rooms and the result appended - and the code reads the already-unwrapped payload rather than .response
the search box is the kit's SearchInput and its onChange is treated as the string it receives, unlike every other kit control whose onChange gives a change event
the sort control is a ComboBox with {key, label} options and selectedOption kept in state
the archived switch is a ToggleButton inside a row with an explicit height, since the control has no intrinsic size
rows are selected with the kit's Checkbox and the select-all checkbox uses isIndeterminate for a partial selection rather than a third visual state of its own

the bulk archive reports progress through addFloatingOperationsButton followed by updateFloatingOperationsButton on the same id - added before updated, since an update on an id that was never added is a silent no-op - and the last update marks the operation completed
each room is archived through the API client and a failure is surfaced as a toast carrying the PluginApiError message, since a plugin's 403 does not navigate the user away
a skeleton or loader renders while the list loads, and a failed load is shown as text rather than thrown, since a throw renders the page as nothing
an empty result renders one of the kit empty-state components - EmptyScreenContainer or EmptyView - or an explicit empty line, not a bare blank area
the people view loads members per room (/files/rooms/{id}/share, or /people) through the same API client and shows each person's role
clicking a room calls navigate() from usePluginActions()

the settings page calls settings.load() in an effect, handles its null (nothing saved yet) instead of destructuring it blindly, and calls settings.setSaveButton() in an effect that re-runs when the form changes
the Save button's isDisabled is tied to both checks - https on the url and a 1-60 number for the minutes - and its onClick awaits settings.save(...)

the settings form is built from FieldContainer units: a TextInput for the url with hasError/errorMessage, a ComboBox of {key, label} environments, a TextInput for the minutes, and the notify ToggleButton in a sized row - no raw <input> or <button>
the EventListener item uses Events.ROOM_CREATE and Events.RENAME or ROOM_EDIT from the enum, and its eventHandler takes no arguments and returns only toasts and update*Items actions
the ArticleButton component is a single IconButton sized 32 that calls navigate() to the page
no hardcoded hex colors - theme variables (--border-service-color for dividers, --text-disable-color for muted text) or the kit's own props instead
items are registered inside onLoadCallback, labels come from a locales module, and item keys are prefixed with the manifest name

evals.name: file-format-and-actions
evals.prompt: we use our own .journal text format at work and docspace just offers download for it. want a plugin that does this properly. clicking a .journal opens it inside docspace with our own icon on the file: you see the text, you can fix a typo right there and put it back, and there's a second view with who owns it and when it last changed so you don't have to leave. there's a way to make a new one - you type the name and it lands in the folder you're looking at. right-clicking one lets you push it to our archive service: it asks for the archive url and a format (zip or tar.gz), complains straight away if the url isn't https, and lets me pick who to notify from the portal's own people list. we often tick ten of them and push the lot at once, and that shouldn't mean ten right-clicks - and again, show it running somewhere. if someone isn't allowed to change a file, don't let them start.
evals.expected_output: A built module plugin with File + MainButton + ContextMenu scopes. The File item claims .journal with the dot and ships a fileRowIcon; its onClick opens an aside whose body is a React component that receives the clicked File through a closure or module variable (useCurrentFile is null there), fetches the text from viewUrl and splits reading from metadata with the kit's Tabs. Editing writes the bytes back with PUT /files/{id}/update and FormData, guarded by the file's own security map, with the Button's isLoading around the await. Creation goes through the portal's create dialog, appending the extension in onSave because the host does not. The archive form is a React modal - dialogBodyComponent - built from the kit: FieldContainer with an https error message, TextInput, ComboBox for the format, a people picker opened with showSelector and closed by hand, a primary Send and a Cancel button in the body. Bulk pushes come from a second, isGroupAction context menu item and report progress through the floating operations button. The archive origin is in cspDomains.
assertions: dist/plugin.zip exists
validate-plugin.mjs --invoke reports zero errors

package.json depends on @onlyoffice/docspace-plugin-sdk 3.x - the npm range ^3.0.0 or the vendored onlyoffice-docspace-plugin-sdk-3.0.0.tgz, which is what the generator writes while the release is unpublished - and declares runtime: module
File, MainButton and ContextMenu scopes are declared, implemented, and each registers at least one item
the File map is keyed by the extension with its leading dot, because the click dispatch matches it against the file's fileExst
a fileRowIcon is shipped - the host uses that one icon at every size outside the tiles view, which reads fileTileIcon instead

the file opens in a surface that is not capped at the default modal 400x280 - an aside (showModal with displayType aside + dialogBodyComponent), the media viewer (showMediaViewer + component), or a modal carrying both autoMaxWidth and autoMaxHeight with a width on the body component root, which is what lifts the cap
the clicked File reaches the viewer component through a module-level variable or a factory, since useCurrentFile() is null in a modal opened from a class-side click
the file's text is read from its viewUrl, not from a URL built by hand

the viewUrl fetch sends no credentials option - viewUrl is a signed off-origin CDN link where the portal stores files in S3, and a credentialed request to its wildcard ACAO is rejected by the browser with a bare Failed to fetch
the text and the metadata are two views rather than one long column - the kit's Tabs with selectedItemId in state, or a dedicated info panel tab for the metadata

the edited text is written back with PUT /files/{id}/update and FormData - the documented replace-contents call - and not with PUT /files/file/{id}, which only renames, nor with PUT /files/file/{id}/saveediting (the api-sdk's saveEditingFileFromForm), which writes the version but leaves the open file list stale
the metadata view reads GET /files/file/{id} through usePluginAPI and renders it with the kit's Text or Link, with no .response access

the portal calls live in per-domain modules that take the PluginAPIClient as an argument and import nothing from react, with usePluginAPI() used only in a thin per-domain hook at the boundary - not api.get() calls spread through the components

editing is gated on the file's own security map (FilesSecurity.Edit) before the control is enabled, and a 403 is still caught and shown as a toast, since a plugin's forbidden answer does not navigate the user away
the save Button uses isLoading around the await so the click cannot be repeated mid-request

the context menu registers two items - a plain one with onItemClick and a separate one with isGroupAction and onGroupClick - because a group item is hidden for single selection and its onItemClick would never fire

the bulk push reports progress through addFloatingOperationsButton and then updateFloatingOperationsButton on the same id, in that order, since an update on an id that was never added is a silent no-op, and the last update marks the operation completed; if cancellation is wired, cancelOperation takes no arguments and stopping everything there is correct, while onCancelOperationFromList receives the id already stripped of the plugin-name prefix and matches it against the running operation
the context menu items are restricted to the extension via fileExt
creation goes through showCreateDialogModal with createDialogProps rather than a hand-built modal, and onSave appends the extension itself - the dialog's extension field only drives the checkbox
the archive form is a React component built from @docspace/ui-kit - FieldContainer, TextInput, ComboBox, Button - with no raw <button> or <input> elements
the https check drives hasError/errorMessage on the FieldContainer or TextInput and disables the primary button

the people to notify come from the portal's People selector - SelectorType.People, opened either from the form with showSelector or from the class-side click with Actions.showSelector - and closeSelector is called from onSubmit and onCancel, since a selector never closes itself
the ComboBox options are {key, label} objects and selectedOption is kept in React state and updated from onSelect
the modal's action row is rendered inside dialogBodyComponent - primary first, then cancel - and closeModal() is called from it

the third-party call goes through fetch rather than the API client, which refuses absolute URLs, and the CSP question is answered rather than ignored: the origin sits in cspDomains (spelled cspDomains, not scpDomains) where it is known at build time, or the run says plainly that a URL typed at runtime cannot be declared statically and names what an administrator has to add
network failures inside components are caught and shown as a toast or text, not left to reject
class-side callbacks (onClick, onItemClick, onSave) catch their own errors and return an IMessage
items are registered inside onLoadCallback and item keys are prefixed with the manifest name

evals.name: extend-room-notes
evals.prompt: here is our room-notes plugin, already installed on the portal and working. two things people keep asking for. first, they want the room's note right there in the room's details panel without opening the dialog, and to edit it in place - but only the people who run the room should be able to change it, the rest just read. while you're in there it helps to see who's actually in the room, so you know who the note is for. second, everyone wants somewhere personal to see every note they've written across rooms at once, with the room names, a box to find one by text, and a click that drops you into the room with its note already open. and when there's nothing yet, say so rather than showing an empty box.
evals.expected_output: The existing project is extended in place: InfoPanel and ProfileMenu added to scopes and implemented together, version bumped, name and pluginName untouched, the existing context menu item still registered, the project's own conventions followed - locales.ts, the exported notes map in NoteModal.tsx, the .tsx component file. The info panel tab is a React component that reads the selected room with useCurrentFile(), edits the note with the kit's Textarea and Button, decides read-only from useCurrentUser() rather than from the item filter, and lists the room's members from /files/rooms/{id}/share with a skeleton while they load. The profile menu item's onClick takes no arguments and opens an aside (showModal, displayType aside, dialogBodyComponent) listing the current user's notes with a SearchInput over them, an EmptyScreenContainer when there are none, and a row click that navigates to the room and opens the plugin's own info panel tab.
assertions: dist/plugin.zip exists and was rebuilt after the edit
validate-plugin.mjs --invoke reports zero errors
InfoPanel and ProfileMenu are added to package.json:scopes and implemented in the same change
name stays room-notes and pluginName stays RoomNotes, since the portal keys the installed plugin by them
version is bumped above the version the project arrived with, without which the portal serves the cached bundle
runtime stays module and the project keeps its Vite config and default export
the existing room-notes-edit context menu item is still registered and still works
the project is edited in place rather than regenerated - locales.ts and NoteModal.tsx survive, labels go through t()
the new surfaces read and write the same exported notes map the modal already uses, rather than starting a second store that would disagree with it

the info panel item is restricted to rooms with filesType [FilesType.room], and if it filters by user role at all it uses usersTypes, the plural form this scope reads - the prompt wants readers to see the tab, so a role filter here is a defect rather than a requirement

the info panel tab is a React component passed as component (no body, no onLoad) that reads the selected room with useCurrentFile() and re-reads when the selection changes, through an effect keyed on the file id
the tab edits the note with the kit's Textarea and saves with a kit Button - no raw <textarea> or <button>

read-only is decided from the room's own security map (Security.EditRoom on the room the panel fetched) rather than from the viewer's portal-wide user type, since being a room admin somewhere does not make you the manager of this room - and it is expressed as isDisabled or isReadOnly on the control rather than by hiding the editor
the room's members are loaded with usePluginAPI() from /files/rooms/{id}/share in an effect with an AbortController, with a skeleton or loader while they load
the members request is abandoned when the selection changes - the effect aborts its controller in the cleanup, so a slow answer for the previous room cannot land in the current one
a room with no note yet renders as an empty note rather than as an error or a spinner that never resolves, since having nothing written is the normal case for this plugin
the tab lays out for the ~337px info panel and adds no scroll container of its own, since the panel already scrolls
the profile menu item registers in the bundle and its onClick takes no arguments; if it filters by user role at all it uses usersType, the singular form this scope reads, never the plural one
the personal view is an aside - showModal with displayType aside and dialogBodyComponent - and never a plain modal, which is 400x280
the aside identifies the current user with useCurrentUser() rather than a hand-made request
the room titles in the aside are resolved through the API (/files/rooms or /files/folder/{id}) in one effect rather than being invented from the stored ids
the aside filters its rows with the kit's SearchInput, whose onChange gives the string itself
an empty personal view renders one of the kit empty-state components - EmptyScreenContainer or EmptyView - or an explicit line of text, not a blank body
a row click calls navigate() to the room and then openInfoPanel with the plugin tab's own key, which is what the action takes to open your own tab
new item keys are namespaced with room-notes and do not collide with the existing one
setLanguage rebuilds the new items alongside the existing one
